name: Kate Parra
life: “I still remember carrying a pattern in my father's hat.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Kate usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I borrowed the pattern for my dad. He wants pockets large enough for Sunday's newspaper.
appearance: Kate is easy to recognize by a loose dark braid and a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Kate folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Kate has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Kate can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To make a newspaper pocket for the father's coat.
family: Hollis Fry is Kate’s half-sibling. Kate sets the time to leave. Hollis picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The wrong bicycle*, Hollis says, “The taped saddle tips to the left because my hip does.”
connections: Judith Hong. They compare the fastenings needed by two different seated wearers.

reactions.situation: The diner wants to fasten the new cuff unaided
reactions.response: Kate leaves the cuff in reach and lets the diner set the pace.

reactions.situation: A traveler asks for the last seat at the bus stop
reactions.response: Kate asks the person already using it whether they can comfortably stand, rather than presuming who needs it most.
